transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-08-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (EdgeCare Head of AI), Mark Tan (EdgeCare SRE), Olivia Chen (EdgeCare Product)

Summary (auto): Quick sync on the latest quality evals; some regressions noted on the new prompt set for discharge summaries; discussed guardrail tuning and next steps for regression runs and security docs.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Samantha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya: Hi Priya here.
[00:08] Mark: Mark, thanks.
[00:09] Olivia: Olivia here.
[00:11] Diego: Diego from Redwood.
[00:12] Samantha: Great, thanks. The plan for today is quick review of the quality evaluation you ran last week on the clinical summarization prompt set, call out any regressions, and pick actions. Diego has the deeper numbers. Diego, over to you.
[00:28] Diego: Cool, yeah so we ran the new prompt set across the 2k holdout cases you provided, plus the previous baseline prompt from last month for comparison. Overall precision is up slightly for medication extraction but we saw a drop in the free-text discharge summary quality score — about a 7% delta in ROUGE-like scoring when we applied the tighter guardrails. So that's likely the regression Priya flagged.
[00:54] Priya: Yeah that's the one — it started to truncate contextual nuance in a few cases, and some of the templated phrasing got more conservative which removed helpful patient context.
[01:06] Samantha: When you say "tighter guardrails" is that the new hallucination filter + conservative temperature change Diego?
[01:12] Diego: Yeah it's two changes: we lowered temperature from 0.7 to 0.5 and enabled the new prefix filter that drops low-confidence tokens on entity spans. Also turned on a mild detokenization normalization that I think made some phrasing more rigid.
[01:28] Olivia: I noticed also that the example where the model omitted comorbidity details was missing an anchor we used previously — so maybe the prompt removed that anchor inadvertently.
[01:36] Diego: That's possible, we did prune some long templates to reduce token cost. There's a trade-off there.
[01:41] Priya: Can we see the side-by-side examples of the top 10 regressions? That's the only way to evaluate whether it's acceptable vs clinically important.
[01:50] Samantha: Yes, we'll send a spreadsheet with the diffs. Diego, can you add the top 10 failures and the example ids?
[01:56] Diego: Yup I'll export the cases and annotate.
[01:59] Mark: On the infra side, I wanted to surface latency — during the larger batch runs we saw tail latency spikes when we hit 16 concurrent streams on your dedicated pool. What's your recommended configuration to avoid those spikes?
[02:11] Diego: Good catch. For those workloads we recommend bumping the batch concurrency to a fixed 12 and enabling the continuous KV cache — that reduces repeated prefix work. Also, if you pin to the dedicated instance family we did a kernel selection that reduces memory churn. We're seeing the tail at around 2200ms for some long contexts, we can get that down to ~1200ms with the cache and slightly different kernel flags.
[02:37] Mark: Okay that sounds reasonable, we'll try the cache and report back. Anything needed from us to enable that?
[02:42] Diego: Just the model version pin and permission to toggle the cache settings — we'll provide an ops-safe playbook.
[02:48] Priya: On scoring, the spreadsheet's score column was a mix of automated ROUGE-ish and a manual clinical relevance annotation from your team. Can you remind me how you compute the combined score?
[02:59] Diego: Sure — it's currently a weighted hybrid: 0.6 automated lexical overlap, 0.4 clinical relevance (human annotations). We can change weights, or introduce precision/recall buckets for medication/entity extraction.
[03:12] Priya: We'd like recall to be favored for meds and allergies — those are safety critical — while summary wording can be precision-biased. So can we get a breakdown by metric?
[03:22] Diego: Absolutely, breaking out by metric is straightforward. I'll include medication/allergy precision/recall and overall summary ROUGE in the next export.
[03:29] Samantha: Great. Also, on the guardrail side Priya, you mentioned hallucination filters — do you want us to soften them or add an explicit "unable to determine" fallback?
[03:40] Priya: I prefer an explicit fallback for any uncertain clinical assertions — so if confidence < threshold it should return "insufficient information" rather than inventing details.
[03:49] Diego: We have a fallback template that does that, but it can sometimes reduce helpful context. There's a tunable confidence threshold; we can run a small sweep to find the knee where hallucinations drop but utility stays acceptable.
[04:00] Olivia: How long would that sweep take?
[04:03] Diego: For 1k cases, about 4–6 hours on dedicated capacity; for the full 2k it takes roughly a day inclusive of post-processing.
[04:12] Priya: Ok let's do a 1k sweep first. If that shows improvement we'll scale.
[04:16] Samantha: Sounds good. Mark — you had a security question earlier about logs and retention?
[04:21] Mark: Yeah, we need audit logs that show per-request redaction and the ability to set retention to 90 days for dev and 365 for prod. Also KMS integration for keys.
[04:31] Samantha: We can share our SOC2 and ISO docs and an ops note that shows how we implement KMS and per-request redaction. We'll include that in the package.
[04:40] Mark: Cool, send to mark.t@edgecare (sic).
[04:44] Samantha: Got it.
[04:46] Priya: One more question on drift/regression alerts — can Redwood trigger automatic regression alerts based on the scoring pipeline?
[04:55] Diego: Yes, we can configure an eval job to run daily and alert if any metric drops > X% or if the top N cases change. We can push to Slack or your monitoring.
[05:07] Priya: Great, we want both slack and email for high severity.
[05:11] Diego: Noted.
[05:13] Samantha: OK let's recap next steps: Diego will run the 1k sweep with softened fallback thresholds and produce a top-10 regression export; Samantha will send the updated prompt set and scoring sheet plus SOC2/ISO docs; Priya to confirm KPI thresholds; Mark to send RBAC/KMS requirements. Any other blockers?
[05:31] Olivia: Pricing — can you confirm pilot extension costs if we need another month?
[05:35] Samantha: Yes I'll include pilot extension pricing tiers in the email — short and long options, plus a dedicated capacity estimate if you want to lock throughput.
[05:43] Priya: One micro note — some of the transcribed examples had minor OCR-ish issues in the labels, so when you send the diffs please include the raw request ids.
[05:53] Diego: Will do.
[05:55] Samantha: Alright thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts by Friday.
[06:01] Priya: Thanks all.
[06:03] Mark: Thanks.
[06:04] Olivia: Bye.

(Transcript ends)

References: prompt-set-v3.xlsx (shared link), quality-scoring-v2.csv (shared), SOC2-summary.pdf (to be shared).
